* The [`Image`] widget has a fixed size in rows/columns. If the image pixel size exceeds the
 pixel area of the rows/columns, the image is scaled down proportionally to "fit" once, at the
 creation time of the [`Protocol`].
 The big upside is that this widget is _stateless_ (in terms of ratatui, i.e. immediate-mode),
 and thus can never block the rendering thread/task. A lot of ratatui apps only use stateless
 widgets, so this factor is also important when chosing.
 What happens when the image does not fit into the render area can be controlled with
 [`Image::allow_clipping`].
* The [StatefulImage] widget adapts to its render area at render-time. It can be set to fit,
 crop, or scale to the available render area.
 This means the widget must be stateful, i.e. use `render_stateful_widget` which takes a
 mutable state parameter.
 The resizing and encoding is blocking, and since it happens at render-time, it should always
 be offloaded to another thread or async task, to keep the UI responsive (see
 `examples/thread.rs` and `examples/tokio.rs` on how to use [`thread::ThreadProtocol`]).

# Plan: Ratatui (TUI) renderer — `pathland-render-tui`

## Feasibility assessment

Ratatui is **immediate-mode** (every terminal frame redraws the whole UI from the retained tree) — a great fit for Pathland's contract: the renderer stays a pure function of the opcode stream and only retains its **rendered-output tree + per-frame geometry cache** (id → Rect) for hit-testing and scroll/focus/cursor state. The transport is a natural fit: implement the existing `Pump` trait (`pathland-render-gtk/src/lib.rs:56-61`), reuse the canonical `RenderTree::apply_frame` decoder, and write inputs back through `Host::send_event` (renderer writes + wakes; **app** drains — same rule as GTK, `pathland-render-gtk/src/lib.rs:49-56`).

### Component → TUI mapping

| Component | Ratatui mapping | Feasibility |
|---|---|---|
| `TEXT` | `Paragraph`/`Line`/`Span` — wrap, `LINE_LIMIT` clamp, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, colors, weight/italic/underline/strike | ✅ native |
| `VSTACK`/`HSTACK`/`LAZY_*` | `Layout` (Vertical/Horizontal) + `Constraint`s from sizes/`SPACING`; eager lazy (spec-permitted) | ✅ native |
| `GRID`/`LAZY_VGRID`/`LAZY_HGRID`/`GRID_ROW` | nested `Layout` split; `GRID_TRACKS` flex/fixed/adaptive → `Constraint::{Fill,Length,Min}`; per-cell 2D placement; no-count → single-track (GTK parity) | ✅ native |
| `ZSTACK` | overlay draws (later = on top), 2D `ALIGNMENT` via per-child cell placement | ✅ native |
| `SCROLLVIEW` | clip child to viewport + `Scrollbar`; retained scroll offset → `SCROLL`/`WHEEL` events | ✅ native |
| `BUTTON` | styled block/paragraph; hover/press via mouse; Enter/Space; `POINTER_UP` on release | ✅ native |
| `SPACER`/`DIVIDER`/`COLOR` | flexible `Constraint` / `─` line / bg-fill area (`Fill` widget) | ✅ native |
| `PROGRESS_VIEW` | `Gauge` (determinate) / animated char spinner (indeterminate) | ✅ native |
| `GAUGE` | `Gauge`/`LineGauge` with min/max | ✅ native |
| `SLIDER` | `LineGauge` + thumb char; arrows/drag → `VALUE_CHANGED` | ✅ native |
| `TOGGLE`/`STEPPER` | `[x]`/switch text; `− value +`; click/keys → `VALUE_CHANGED` | ✅ native |
| `TEXT_FIELD`/`TEXT_EDITOR` | `Paragraph` + cursor; typing → `TEXT_CHANGED`; focus → `FOCUS_CHANGED`; Enter → `SUBMIT` | ✅ native |
| `PICKER`/`MENU` | `List` selectable / popup overlay `List` | ✅ native |
| `DATE_PICKER` | `calendar::Monthly` widget → `DATE_CHANGED` | ✅ native |
| `SHAPE` | `Canvas`/block chars (rect/circle/capsule approximation) | ⚠️ approximation |
| `IMAGE` | `ratatui-image` (Sixel/Kitty/iTerm2 + halfblock fallback) | ⚠️ feature-gated, terminal-dependent |
| `COLOR_PICKER` | swatch + hex edit | ⚠️ deferred |
| `AUDIO`/`VIDEO` | status line only (no terminal media) | ❌ out of scope |

### Property handling
Colors → Ratatui `Color` (16/256/truecolor); `FONT_WEIGHT`→Bold, `FONT_STYLE`→italic, `UNDERLINE`/`STRIKETHROUGH`→line styles; `FONT_SIZE`/`BORDER_RADIUS`/`SHADOW_*`/`BLUR`/`ROTATION`/`SCALE`/`OPACITY` → ignored (renderer fidelity choice, like other renderers); `VISIBLE` → skip draw; `CLIPS_TO_BUFFERS` → natural; `PADDING`/`CONTENT_MARGINS` → area insets; `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` `FILL`/`HUG` → `Constraint`; `ALIGNMENT` 2D → cell placement (reuse `align_h`/`align_v`, `effective_fill`, `grid_cells` from `pathland-render-gtk/src/layout.rs` — all display-free, pure decisions). Design tokens: reuse `pathland_core::tokens::resolve` + a per-renderer default table + `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides.

## Architecture

**New crate** `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-tui/` (workspace member, **rlib only** — a TUI is a Rust-only surface, no cdylib/JNA), deps: `pathland-core`, `pathland-core-transport`, `ratatui 0.30` (+ crossterm 0.29 backend, default). Modules:
- `host.rs` — the retained `RenderTree`/`HostNode` decoder + token resolution (see decision below).
- `layout.rs` — TUI layout: stack/grid/zstack rects, alignment, fill/hug → `Layout`+`Constraint` (mirrors GTK `layout.rs`, headless-testable).
- `draw.rs` — recursive widget pass over the tree → ratatui widgets into the `Frame`'s areas; keeps `HashMap<u32, Rect>` per frame for hit-testing.
- `input.rs` — crossterm event → protocol `Event` (`POINTER_*`, `KEY_*`, `WHEEL`, `VALUE_CHANGED`, `TEXT_CHANGED`, …), gated by `EVENT_LISTENERS`/`BINDING_ID`; key-code table (ASCII + special-key constants, documented in `spec/EVENTS.md`).
- `run.rs` — event loop: `next_frame()` → apply → `terminal.draw(draw)`; on input `send_input` + wake; the host (app) drains. `Pump` impls over `RingTransport` (mirrors `pump_once`).
- Demo `pathland-render-tui-demo` mirroring `pathland-render-gtk-demo`: DSL → `Engine` → ring → renderer → crossterm loop → drain → app state → re-emit.
- `status.md` per AGENTS.md; headless tests via Ratatui's **`TestBackend`**.

## Milestones (each ends green + committed)

- **M0 — Scaffold**: crate + workspace entry + `status.md`; shared decoder decision; `cargo build`/`test` green.
- **M1 — Static rendering**: stacks, `TEXT`, `SPACER`/`DIVIDER`/`COLOR`, `BUTTON` visual, `PROGRESS_VIEW`/`GAUGE`; spacing/padding/alignment/FILL; `TestBackend` golden tests; static demo renders a counter.
- **M2 — Interaction**: mouse hit-testing, keyboard + focus model, event write/wake + app drain; `BUTTON` click, `TOGGLE`/`SLIDER`/`STEPPER` value changes, `TEXT_FIELD` input; interactive demo.
- **M3 — Layout depth**: `GRID`/`GRID_ROW`/`GRID_TRACKS`, `ZSTACK` overlay, `SCROLLVIEW`+`Scrollbar`+`SCROLL`/`WHEEL`, `PICKER`/`MENU`/`DATE_PICKER`, `SHAPE` canvas.
- **M4 — Tokens + resize + polish**: token tables (light/dark) + overrides, terminal resize → `META::ENVIRONMENT` (app-side emit on SIGWINCH), key-code spec note, conformance/golden buffers, docs.
- **M5 (optional)** — `IMAGE` via `ratatui-image` behind a feature; media status line.

## Key risks / non-negotiables
- Terminal is cell-based: no pixels, no effects, images only via graphics protocols.
- Hit-testing depends on a fresh id→Rect map each frame — must be rebuilt in the same pass as drawing.
- The `no_std`/wasm32 guard is unaffected (renderer is std; core untouched).
- Renderer statelessness (AGENTS.md Principle 1): only output-tree + geometry + input-focus/scroll cursor retained; scroll/cursor are rendered-output state, app owns all logic.

Two decisions to confirm before I finalize:

All three confirmed. Here's the finalized plan.

## Final plan — Ratatui renderer (`pathland-render-tui`)

### Phase M0 — Shared host reader + scaffold
1. **New crate `lib/rust/crates/pathland-host/`** (std, dep: `pathland-core`; workspace member): move `HostNode`, `RenderTree`, `apply_frame`, `resolve_tokens`, `render_tree_from_frame` out of `pathland-render-gtk/src/host.rs` (lines 17–288) **unchanged** and `pub`. This is pure protocol decoding + `pathland_core::tokens` resolution — no GTK types. Keep `describe`, `concrete_default_tables`, and GTK token enrichment in `render-gtk` (renderer-owned defaults stay per-renderer).
2. **Refactor `pathland-render-gtk`** to depend on `pathland-host` (update `use`s in `lib.rs`, delete the moved code, re-export `RenderTree` for compat if needed). `cargo test -p pathland-render-gtk` must stay green — this is a move, no behavior change.
3. **New crate `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-tui/`** (rlib only — no cdylib, TUI is a Rust surface): deps `pathland-core`, `pathland-core-transport`, `pathland-host`, `ratatui = "0.30"` (default crossterm backend). Empty module skeleton + `status.md` + workspace entry. `cargo build`/`test` green.

### Phase M1 — Static rendering (first implementation slice)
1. **`layout.rs`** — TUI layout decisions (headless-testable): `align_h`/`align_v`/`align_from` and `effective_fill`/`fills_axis` logic ported from `pathland-render-gtk/src/layout.rs` but producing ratatui `Rect`/`Constraint` (stacks → `Layout` + `Constraint::{Fill,Length,Min}`; padding/margins → area insets; `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` `FILL`/`HUG` → constraints; 1 pt ≈ 1 cell).
2. **`draw.rs`** — recursive pass over the retained `RenderTree` into the ratatui `Frame`: `TEXT`→`Paragraph` (colors, weight, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `LINE_LIMIT`/truncation), `VSTACK`/`HSTACK`/`LAZY_*`, `SPACER`/`DIVIDER`/`COLOR`, `BUTTON` visual block, `PROGRESS_VIEW` (`Gauge`/spinner), `GAUGE`. Also builds the per-frame `HashMap<u32, Rect>` for later hit-testing.
3. **`render.rs`** — `apply_frame` via the shared `RenderTree`; a `draw()` entry point; a static demo (`pathland-render-tui-demo`, mirroring `pathland-render-gtk-demo`) that emits a counter tree via the DSL → `Engine` → `RingTransport` and renders it.
4. **Tests**: `TestBackend` golden-buffer tests for stacks/text/spacing/alignment/fill; demo `cargo run` visual check (on your display).
5. **Verify**: `cargo test` (full workspace), `npm test` unaffected, commit.

### Phase M2 — Interaction
Crossterm event loop → protocol `Event`: mouse hit-test via the retained id→Rect map → `POINTER_*`; keyboard + focus model → `KEY_*` (key-code table documented in `spec/EVENTS.md`); `BUTTON` click, `TOGGLE`/`SLIDER`/`STEPPER` → `VALUE_CHANGED`; `TEXT_FIELD` → `TEXT_CHANGED`/`FOCUS_CHANGED`/`SUBMIT`. `Pump` over `RingTransport`: `next_frame` + `send_input` + wake; **app drains** (GTK rule). `EVENT_LISTENERS`/`BINDING_ID` gating. Interactive demo (counter + controls).

### Phase M3 — Layout depth
`GRID`/`GRID_ROW`/`GRID_TRACKS` (→ `Constraint` split), `ZSTACK` overlay + 2D alignment, `SCROLLVIEW` + `Scrollbar` + retained scroll offset → `SCROLL`/`WHEEL`, `PICKER`/`MENU` (`List`/popup), `DATE_PICKER` (`calendar::Monthly`), `SHAPE` canvas approximation.

### Phase M4 — Tokens, resize, polish
TUI token tables (light/dark) + `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides via `pathland_core::tokens::resolve`; terminal resize → `META::ENVIRONMENT` (app-side emit on SIGWINCH); `status.md`; golden/conformance tests; docs.

### Phase M5 — optional, feature-gated
`IMAGE` via `ratatui-image` (sixel/Kitty/iTerm2 + halfblock fallback) behind a feature flag; `COLOR_PICKER` swatch/hex; `AUDIO`/`VIDEO` status line.

### Out of scope / risks
Effects (`SHADOW_*`/`BLUR`/`ROTATION`/`SCALE`), `FONT_SIZE`, `BORDER_RADIUS`, `OPACITY` — ignored (renderer fidelity, per protocol). `no_std`/wasm guard unaffected. Statelessness: only output tree + geometry + input focus/scroll cursors retained.

Ready to start M0 on your go.

141:     /// Re-resolve every `DESIGN_TOKEN`-typed property against the theme, the
142:     /// active scheme, and the parent-fallback chain, materializing concrete
143:     /// values into [`HostNode::properties`] (numeric) or [`HostNode::strings`]
144:     /// (STRING tokens). The paths are kept in [`HostNode::token_refs`] for
145:     /// re-resolution on scheme change.
146:     pub fn resolve_tokens(&mut self) {
147:         let tables = TokenTables {
148:             overrides: &self.overrides,
149:             dark_overrides: &self.dark_overrides,
150:             defaults: &self.defaults,
151:             dark_defaults: &self.dark_defaults,
152:         };
153:         for node in self.nodes.values_mut() {
154:             let refs: Vec<(u16, String)> = node.token_refs.iter().map(|(k, v)| (*k, v.clone())).collect();
155:             for (prop, path) in refs {
156:                 if let Some(value) = resolve_token(&path, self.scheme, &tables) {
157:                     match value {
158:                         TokenValue::Str(s) => {
159:                             node.strings.insert(prop, s);
160:                         }
161:                         _ => {
162:                             if let Some(bits) = value.to_bits() {
163:                                 node.properties.insert(prop, bits);
164:                             }
165:                         }
166:                     }
167:                 }
168:             }
169:         }
170:     }

172:     /// Apply a frame's opcodes to this tree (a delta).
173:     pub fn apply_frame(&mut self, frame: &Frame<'_>) {
174:         for op in frame.opcodes() {
175:             match (op.category(), op.command()) {
176:                 (category::TREE, tree::CREATE_NODE) => {
177:                     let id = op.a();
178:                     let ty = op.b() as u16;
179:                     let entry = self.nodes.entry(id).or_default();
180:                     entry.id = id;
181:                     entry.component_type = ty;
182:                 }
183:                 (category::TREE, tree::DELETE_NODE) => {
184:                     self.nodes.remove(&op.a());
185:                 }
186:                 (category::TREE, tree::INSERT_CHILD) => {
187:                     let (parent, child) = (op.a(), op.b());
188:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
189:                         if !p.children.contains(&child) {
190:                             p.children.push(child);
191:                         }
192:                     }
193:                     if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
194:                         c.parent = Some(parent);
195:                     }
196:                 }
197:                 (category::TREE, tree::REMOVE_CHILD) => {
198:                     let (parent, child) = (op.a(), op.b());
199:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
200:                         p.children.retain(|c| *c != child);
201:                     }
202:                     if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
203:                         c.parent = None;
204:                     }
205:                 }
206:                 (category::TREE, tree::MOVE_CHILD) => {
207:                     let (parent, child, new_index) = (op.a(), op.b(), op.c() as usize);
208:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
209:                         if let Some(pos) = p.children.iter().position(|c| *c == child) {
210:                             p.children.remove(pos);
211:                         }
212:                         let idx = if new_index == usize::MAX {
213:                             p.children.len()
214:                         } else {
215:                             new_index.min(p.children.len())
216:                         };
217:                         p.children.insert(idx, child);
218:                     }
219:                 }
220:                 (category::PARAMETER, parameter::SET_PROPERTY) => {
221:                     let prop_id = op.b() as u16;
222:                     let vt = (op.b() >> 16) as u8;
223:                     if let Some(n) = self.nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
224:                         if vt == value_type::STRING {
225:                             // Resolve the arena offset into the actual text.
226:                             if let Ok(text) = frame.arena_str(op.c()) {
227:                                 n.strings.insert(prop_id, text.to_string());
228:                             }
229:                         } else if vt == value_type::DESIGN_TOKEN {
230:                             // A token reference: keep the path for resolution
231:                             // against the theme (spec/TOKENS.md). C is the arena
232:                             // offset of the token path.
233:                             if let Ok(path) = frame.arena_str(op.c()) {
234:                                 n.token_refs.insert(prop_id, path.to_string());
235:                             }
236:                         } else {
237:                             n.properties.insert(prop_id, op.c());
238:                         }
239:                     }
240:                 }
241:                 (category::PARAMETER, parameter::SET_TEXT) => {
242:                     if let Some(n) = self.nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
243:                         n.text = frame.arena_str(op.b()).ok().map(|s| s.to_string());
244:                     }
245:                 }
246:                 (category::PARAMETER, parameter::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN) => {
247:                     // Global override: A = arenaRef (token path), B = valueType,
248:                     // C = value (for STRING, an arenaRef to the value string).
249:                     if let Ok(path) = frame.arena_str(op.a()) {
250:                         let vt = (op.b() & 0xFF) as u8;
251:                         let value = if vt == value_type::STRING {
252:                             frame
253:                                 .arena_str(op.c())
254:                                 .map(|s| TokenValue::Str(s.to_string()))
255:                                 .unwrap_or(TokenValue::U32(0))
256:                         } else {
257:                             TokenValue::from_wire(vt, op.c()).unwrap_or(TokenValue::U32(op.c()))
258:                         };
259:                         if let Some(bare) = path.strip_prefix("dark.") {
260:                             self.dark_overrides.insert(bare.to_string(), value);
261:                         } else {
262:                             self.overrides.insert(path.to_string(), value);
263:                         }
264:                     }
265:                 }
266:                 _ => {}
267:             }
268:         }
269:         self.resolve_tokens();
270:     }

398: /// Convert a single opcode into a human-readable line (debugging aid).
399: pub fn describe(op: &Opcode) -> String {
400:     match (op.category(), op.command()) {
401:         (category::TREE, tree::CREATE_NODE) => {
402:             format!("TREE:CREATE_NODE id={} type=0x{:04x}", op.a(), op.b() as u16)
403:         }
404:         (category::TREE, tree::DELETE_NODE) => format!("TREE:DELETE_NODE id={}", op.a()),
405:         (category::TREE, tree::INSERT_CHILD) => format!(
406:             "TREE:INSERT_CHILD parent={} child={} index={}",
407:             op.a(),
408:             op.b(),
409:             op.c()
410:         ),
411:         (category::TREE, tree::REMOVE_CHILD) => {
412:             format!("TREE:REMOVE_CHILD parent={} child={}", op.a(), op.b())
413:         }
414:         (category::TREE, tree::MOVE_CHILD) => format!(
415:             "TREE:MOVE_CHILD parent={} child={} index={}",
416:             op.a(),
417:             op.b(),
418:             op.c()
419:         ),
420:         (category::PARAMETER, parameter::SET_PROPERTY) => format!(
421:             "PARAMETER:SET_PROPERTY id={} prop=0x{:04x} value=0x{:08x}",
422:             op.a(),
423:             op.b() as u16,
424:             op.c()
425:         ),
426:         (category::PARAMETER, parameter::SET_TEXT) => {
427:             format!("PARAMETER:SET_TEXT id={} arenaRef={}", op.a(), op.b())
428:         }
429:         (category::PARAMETER, parameter::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN) => format!(
430:             "PARAMETER:SET_DESIGN_TOKEN pathArenaRef={} valueType=0x{:02x} value=0x{:08x}",
431:             op.a(),
432:             op.b() & 0xFF,
433:             op.c()
434:         ),
435:         _ => format!("{:?}", op),
436:     }
437: }

4: //! Tier-1 defaults start as **concrete platform-appropriate fallbacks**
5: //! ([`concrete_default_tables`]); when a real widget exists, the tokens the
6: //! current GTK theme can resolve are replaced with **native colors** via
7: //! `gtk::StyleContext::lookup_color` of the theme's named colors (`@theme_*`,
8: //! `@borders`, `@success_color`, …). Headless / theme-missing → pure concrete
9: //! fallback, which keeps tests deterministic.

21:     ("theme_bg_color", "color.background"),

30:     ("warning_color", "color.warning"),

36: pub fn scheme_from_settings(settings: &gtk::Settings) -> Scheme {
37:     let dark = settings.is_gtk_application_prefer_dark_theme()
38:         || settings
39:             .gtk_theme_name()
40:             .as_deref()
41:             .map_or(false, |name| name.ends_with("-dark"));
42:     if dark {
43:         Scheme::Dark

52: /// only the *active* scheme's defaults are native; the other scheme keeps its
53: /// concrete fallback.
54: pub fn enrich_defaults<F>(
55:     resolve: &F,
56:     scheme: Scheme,

59:     F: Fn(&str) -> Option<u32>,
60: {
61:     let (mut base, mut dark) = concrete_default_tables();
62:     let target = match scheme {
63:         Scheme::Dark => &mut dark,
64:         Scheme::Light => &mut base,
65:     };

67:         if let Some(argb) = resolve(name) {

# pathland-render-tui — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 2, 2026

The **Ratatui (TUI) renderer**: maps opcode frames incrementally onto native
terminal widgets (immediate-mode redraw each terminal frame). Protocol contract:
`spec/`. Retained-tree decoding + token resolution come from the shared
`pathland-host` crate.

## Implemented

- **Components → widgets** (`render.rs`):
  - `VSTACK`/`HSTACK`/`LAZY_VSTACK`/`LAZY_HSTACK` → ratatui `Layout` (spacing/
    padding/`ALIGNMENT` cross-axis, `FILL`/greedy children split leftover on the
    main axis),
  - `TEXT` → `Paragraph` (per-line `Span`s; `COLOR`/`BACKGROUND_COLOR`/
    `FONT_WEIGHT`/`FONT_STYLE`/`UNDERLINE`/`STRIKETHROUGH` styles; `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`;
    `LINE_LIMIT` truncation),
  - `BUTTON` → `Paragraph` + `Block` border (`BORDER_WIDTH`/`BORDER_COLOR`);
    composite bodies render as a horizontal row,
  - `SPACER` → flexible `Constraint`; `DIVIDER` → `─` line; `COLOR` → `Fill`
    background,
  - `PROGRESS_VIEW` → `Gauge` (determinate) / animated braille spinner
    (indeterminate), `GAUGE` → `LineGauge` (`VALUE`/`MIN_VALUE`/`MAX_VALUE`).
- **Layout** (`layout.rs`, pure + headless-testable): bottom-up natural cell
  size, top-down `Rect` assignment; per-edge `PADDING` (`PADDING_*` > `PADDING`
  > `CONTENT_MARGINS`), `SPACING` gaps, 2D `ALIGNMENT` → cross-axis position
  (`align_h`/`align_v`, codes 0–8), `FILL`/`HUG`/Fixed `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`, greedy
  primitives (`SPACER`/`COLOR`/`SCROLLVIEW`). 1 protocol point = 1 cell.
- **Per-frame geometry cache**: `id → Rect` (`TuiRenderer::rect`) for
  hit-testing; rebuilt every draw.
- **Retained-tree decoding** via `pathland_host::RenderTree` (`apply_frame`),
  incl. `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides + token refs; `TuiRenderer::set_scheme`
  re-resolves on scheme change.
- **Demo** (`pathland-render-tui-demo`): DSL → `Engine` → shared ring →
  renderer; quits on `q`/`Esc`/`Ctrl+C`.

## Not implemented / gaps

- **No input yet** (M2 planned): mouse hit-testing → `POINTER_*`, keyboard →
  `KEY_*`, `VALUE_CHANGED`/`TEXT_CHANGED` from controls, `EVENT_LISTENERS`/
  `BINDING_ID` gating, event write + wake/drain loop.
- **No grid/ZStack/ScrollView yet** (M3 planned): `GRID`/`GRID_ROW`/
  `GRID_TRACKS`, `ZSTACK` overlay + 2D alignment, `SCROLLVIEW` + `Scrollbar` +
  `SCROLL`/`WHEEL`, `PICKER`/`MENU`/`DATE_PICKER`, `SHAPE`.
- **No design-token default tables for TUI colors** yet (`SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`
  overrides decode, but `COLOR`-token refs resolve to the shared `pathland-host`
  concrete defaults; a TUI-specific table + scheme detection is a follow-up).
- **No terminal-resize reporting** (`META::ENVIRONMENT` viewport) — the app
  re-draws to `frame.area()` automatically, but the guest is not notified.
- **`IMAGE`** deferred (feature-gated `ratatui-image`, M5); **`AUDIO`/`VIDEO`**
  out of scope (status line only); effects (`SHADOW_*`/`BLUR`/`ROTATION`/
  `SCALE`/`OPACITY`) and `FONT_SIZE`/`BORDER_RADIUS` ignored (renderer fidelity).

## Verified by

`cargo test -p pathland-render-tui` — layout decisions (stack placement,
spacing gaps, filler absorption, `FILL` stretch, cross-axis alignment, padding)
and `TestBackend` buffer assertions (text, spacing, button border, fill color,
gauge ratio). `cargo run -p pathland-render-tui-demo` for a visual check.

So the interactive slice needs just buttons + sliders; the rest renders as placeholders. # Plan: run the Java music-player demo on the TUI renderer ## Feasibility Mirror the GTK host path 1:1: Java DSL mounts `MusicPlayerView` → `Emitter`/`RenderResult` → shared `libpathland_core` ring → Rust renderer pumps the ring in place → inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes → host drains + dispatches via `InputDispatcher`. No `-XstartOnFirstThread`, no GTK, no media assets. ## Work items **1. Rust `pathland-render-tui` M2 — interactive input (bulk of the work)** - **Input mapping** (`render.rs`): crossterm mouse down/up/move/drag → `POINTER_DOWN`/`UP`/`MOVE` (hit-test the per-frame `id→Rect` cache, draw-order = z-order); mouse wheel → `WHEEL`. Keyboard: Tab focus cycling, Enter/Space activates the focused button (synthesized `POINTER_DOWN`+`UP` so the app's `TapRecognizer` fires), arrows adjust slider → `VALUE_CHANGED`, typing → `TEXT_CHANGED`/`SUBMIT`. - **Gating** (GTK parity): `EVENT_LISTENERS` bits gate pointer/key/wheel (buttons default to pointer listeners); `BINDING_ID` gates value/text events. - **Focus model**: single `focus: Option`, Tab cycling, REVERSED focus indicator, cursor for text fields. - **Control rendering** (needed to exercise the shared views robustly): `SLIDER` (LineGauge + value), `TOGGLE` (`[x]`), `STEPPER` (`− v +`), `TEXT_FIELD`/`TEXT_EDITOR` (Paragraph + cursor) + `natural_size` entries in `layout.rs`. - **`run` event loop** over a `Pump` (`FrameSource`+`DriverTransport`, `Rc>` like GTK): apply frames → draw → poll/route input → `send_input` + wake; raw mode + alt-screen setup/teardown; quit on `q`/Ctrl+C, Esc → `Event::Navigate{None}`. - **cdylib + `capi.rs`**: `pathland_tui_run_ring(ring: *mut c_void, on_event: Option)` borrowing a `*mut RingTransport` via a `CoreRingHandle` pump (exact mirror of `pathland_gtk_run_ring`). - **Tests**: TestBackend hit-test / click-routing / arrow-value tests. **2. Rust demo**: wire the counter interactive via `run` + `TapRecognizer` (mirror `pathland-render-gtk-demo`). **3. Java `pathland-tui-demo` module** (mirror `pathland-gtk-demo`): - `TuiRendererNative` (JNA: `pathland_tui_run_ring`), `TuiHost` (mount `MusicPlayerView`, `InputDispatcher` + `RingEventReader` onEvent drain/dispatch, runRing), copied `RingEventReader` (self-contained). - pom.xml + reactor entry in `lib/java/pom.xml`. Run via `mvn -q compile exec:java` with `-Dpathland.core.lib` + `-Dpathland.tui.lib` pointing at `lib/rust/target/debug`. **4. Script** `run-java-tui-demo.sh` + README/AGENTS rows. **5. Verify**: `cargo test` (full workspace incl. M2 tests), `cargo build -p pathland-render-tui` (+ `nm` symbol check for `pathland_tui_run_ring`), `mvn -q install`, then a terminal run on your display (Rust counter + Java music player). ## First-run gaps (documented, not blockers) - **Image** (album covers) + **Audio** (playback): no terminal equivalent — render as empty placeholders; the app logic (buttons, volume/seek sliders) is unaffected. - **ScrollView** (track list): renders its first child at natural size (no scrolling yet — `SCROLL`/`WHEEL` scrolling is M3). - Mouse + arrow-key interaction works; keyboard-only flow is Tab/Enter. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the Java + Ratatui (TUI) desktop demo: the shared MusicPlayerView under
# the native TUI renderer, over the libpathland_core shared ring.
#
# Quit with q or Ctrl+C. No window/display needed — run inside any terminal.
set -euo pipefail
source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/lib.sh"

# Build the Rust dylibs the demo links: the core ring (libpathland_core) and
# the TUI renderer (libpathland_render_tui).
(cd "$ROOT/lib/rust" && cargo build -p pathland-core-capi -p pathland-render-tui)
java_install

case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin)  EXT=".dylib" ;;
  Linux)   EXT=".so" ;;
  MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*) EXT=".dll" ;;
  *) echo "unsupported OS: $(uname -s)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

cd "$ROOT/lib/java/pathland-tui-demo"

CPFILE="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$CPFILE"' EXIT
mvn -q dependency:build-classpath -Dmdep.outputFile="$CPFILE"
CP="target/classes:$(cat "$CPFILE")"

exec java \
  -Dpathland.core.lib="$ROOT/lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_core$EXT" \
  -Dpathland.tui.lib="$ROOT/lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_render_tui$EXT" \
  -cp "$CP" com.pathland.demo.tui.TuiHost

41: - The renderer reports an event for a node **only if that node declared it**
42:   wants it, via the `EVENT_LISTENERS` semantic property (`0x2005`, a u32
43:   bitmask, `SET_PROPERTY` with the `U32` value type). This makes **any element**
44:   (a `Text`, a `VStack`, …) able to emit events, not just controls.
45: 
46: ### Transport-aware event guards (MUST)
47: 
48: Renderers **MUST** implement event guards to prevent network noise. A user
49: interaction — tap, text change, drag, value edit — **MUST NEVER** produce an
50: outbound event opcode unless the target node explicitly declared intent in **at
51: least one** of these ways:
52: 
53: 1. it set the matching `EVENT_LISTENERS` (0x2005) bits, **or**
54: 2. it is a **value-bearing control** reporting by component type (`SLIDER`,
55:    `TOGGLE`, `PICKER`, `MENU`, `DATE_PICKER`, `COLOR_PICKER`, …), **or**
56: 3. it carries a bound callback property — `ACTION_ID` (0x2016) or `BINDING_ID`
57:    (0x2017) — that identifies where the interaction must be routed.
58: 
59: Interactions that match none of these are **dropped at the renderer**; they are
60: never serialized to the event ring or a network batch. This is the wire-level
61: guard: a `Button` tap with no `ACTION_ID`, no `BINDING_ID`, and no
62: `EVENT_LISTENERS` produces no events.
63: 
64: ### Target resolution
65:

Research complete. Here's the picture and plan.

## Root cause
Every renderer applies inbound `VALUE` (`SET_PROPERTY`) to a value control **even while the user is actively dragging it**:
- GTK `pathland-render-gtk/src/lib.rs:409` → `scale.set_value(value)` unconditionally.
- TS DOM client `lib/typescript/src/apply.ts:942` → `range.value = ...` unconditionally (live `input` events sent at `index.ts:426`).
- TUI: sliders only adjust via arrows today (no mouse drag yet), so no flicker yet — but the same hazard exists.

The drag emits `VALUE_CHANGED` → server updates → echoes `SET_PROPERTY VALUE` → the renderer snaps the thumb while the pointer is still moving → **flicker** (and the echoed write re-fires the change signal, today only broken by app-side signal-equality suppression + GTK's idle-pump deferral).

## Fix — renderer-side "in-flight interaction" suppression (all three renderers)
While a value control has an **in-flight user drag**, the renderer:
- does **not** apply inbound `VALUE` to the control's *displayed* position (the drag position wins),
- therefore does **not** re-report `VALUE_CHANGED` for skipped writes (no change signal fires),
- still applies structural props (`MIN`/`MAX`/`STEP`).

On release the in-flight state clears; the final `VALUE_CHANGED` was already sent, and subsequent app updates apply normally. This is transient input/rendered-output state (same category as scroll offset / focus / cursor), so it stays within AGENTS.md Principle 1.

## Work items
1. **Spec** — `spec/EVENTS.md`: add a short "In-flight interaction (MUST)" subsection under the existing transport guards (line 46): the renderer must not apply inbound `VALUE` to a control with an active user interaction, and must not re-report for skipped writes.
2. **GTK** — in-flight drag set (`Rc<RefCell<HashSet<u32>>>` by node id); attach a capture-phase `GestureClick` to the `GtkScale` in `build_widget` (the existing capture trick at `lib.rs:1591`) to add/remove on press/release; skip `set_value` while dragging in `update` (`lib.rs:399`). Add a pure-decision test (`should_apply_value(dragging)`); GTK interaction wiring is headless-tested via the decision fn.
3. **TS DOM client** — module-level `WeakSet<HTMLInputElement>` of in-flight ranges; `pointerdown` adds, `pointerup`/`pointercancel`/`blur` removes (`index.ts`); `apply.ts:942` skips `range.value = ...` for in-flight inputs. Add a test (mark in-flight → apply delta → unchanged; clear → applies).

Confirmed — and this generalizes the design. Current state across renderers:

- **TS client already emits** `FOCUS_CHANGED`/`EDITING_CHANGED` on focus in/out (`index.ts:318-328`) but has **no suppression**: `input.value = text` (`apply.ts:822`) and `range.value` (`apply.ts:942`) apply every inbound delta unconditionally.

- **TUI** re-renders from `node.text`/`VALUE` each frame, so an echoed delta shows immediately while typing/dragging.

## Generalized plan — "in-flight interaction" suppression (not slider-specific)

**The rule (renderer contract):** a node with an **active continuous-input session** keeps its in-edit state user-authoritative — the renderer MUST NOT apply inbound updates to that state while the session lasts, and MUST NOT re-report events for suppressed writes. On session end, inbound updates apply again.

**Two layers:**

**A. Renderer-side suppression of the in-edit state** (fixes the visible flicker):
- *Value drag* (`SLIDER`): suppress inbound `VALUE` while a drag session is active — GTK (capture `GestureClick` → in-flight set → skip `set_value`, `lib.rs:399`), TS (in-flight `WeakSet` → skip `range.value`, `apply.ts:942`), TUI (active-value guard).
- *Text editing* (`TEXT_FIELD`/`TEXT_EDITOR`): suppress inbound `SET_TEXT` while an editing session is active (first typed char after focus → blur) so the caret/composition never jumps — GTK (skip `entry.set_text` while editing), TS (skip `input.value = text` while editing), TUI (keep the in-progress typed text for display). Text-editor equality guard stays as a first-level filter.
- The transient in-edit state (drag position, in-progress text) is input/rendered-output state — permitted by Principle 1, same category as scroll offset/cursor.

**B. Session-boundary events — the general escape hatch for "any widget"**: the protocol already drafts `FOCUS_CHANGED` (0x08) / `EDITING_CHANGED` (0x09). Renderers report them at session start/end so **apps can suppress echoing any derived state** (a pointer-drag offset, a custom-drawn position — which the renderer can't know about). TS already emits them; GTK/TUI would add emission, gated by the existing `LISTEN_FOCUS`/`LISTEN_EDITING` bits (1<<5 / 1<<6). This is what makes the fix general beyond the built-in controls.

**Spec** — `spec/EVENTS.md`: a generalized **"In-flight interaction (MUST)"** section (superseding my earlier slider-only note): the suppression rule + the session-boundary events as the contract.

**Coverage per renderer:** GTK + TS get A (value + text) + B (GTK adds FOCUS/EDITING emission); TUI gets the guard infra for A (value + text), no drag scrubbing, B deferred.

Interactions that match none of these are **dropped at the renderer**; they are
never serialized to the event ring or a network batch. This is the wire-level
guard: a `Button` tap with no `ACTION_ID`, no `BINDING_ID`, and no
`EVENT_LISTENERS` produces no events.

### In-flight interaction (MUST)

A node with an **active continuous-input session** — a slider being dragged, a
text input being typed into, a pointer-drag the app is following — is the
authoritative owner of the state it is editing. Renderers **MUST** honor this
for the duration of the session:

1. **Do not apply inbound updates to the in-edit state.** While the session is
   active, a `SET_PROPERTY` of the state under edit (e.g. `VALUE` (0x2006) on a
   `SLIDER` being dragged) is **skipped at the renderer** — the interaction's
   position wins, so a server echo cannot fight the pointer and cause flicker.
   Structural properties (`MIN_VALUE`/`MAX_VALUE`/`STEP_VALUE`, size, style)
   still apply.
2. **Do not re-report events for skipped writes.** Because the write was not
   applied, no change signal fires and no `VALUE_CHANGED` is re-emitted — the
   echo loop is broken at the source.
3. **Resume on session end.** When the interaction ends (release / blur), the
   in-flight state clears and inbound updates apply again; the final position
   was already reported by the interaction's own events.

This is **renderer state, not application state** (AGENTS.md Principle 1): the
in-edit value is transient input/rendered-output state, like the scroll offset
and the text caret.

The session boundaries are also **reported as events** so the application can
suppress echoes of *derived* state the renderer cannot know about (a custom
drag offset, a drawn position):

- `FOCUS_CHANGED` (0x08) — the control gained/lost focus.
- `EDITING_CHANGED` (0x09) — a value/text edit session started/ended.

Both are reported **only when the target declared the matching `EVENT_LISTENERS`
bit** (`FOCUS` = `1<<5`, `EDITING` = `1<<6`). An application that observes
`EDITING_CHANGED { editing: true }` should hold back authoritative echoes of the
edited state until `{ editing: false }`.

The mechanism is **per-state / per-session**: implemented today for value drags
(`SLIDER`); text editing and other continuous inputs use the same path.

content.text:
Investigation done — I found a concrete, code-grounded bug that matches "the seekbar is broken."

## The seekbar bug: signal handlers stack on every sync

`update()` runs on **every sync** for every node (`sync_node` → `update`, `lib.rs:233`), and it calls `attach_control_events(...)` (`lib.rs:351`). Unlike `attach_listeners` (guarded by `attached_listeners`) and my new `attach_drag_sessions` (guarded by `attached_sessions`), **`attach_control_events` has no idempotency guard** (`lib.rs:484`) — it calls `scale.connect_value_changed(...)` unconditionally for any slider with a `BINDING_ID`.

So every echoed frame during a drag (or every `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` during playback) attaches **another** `value_changed` handler. One drag motion then fires N handlers → N `VALUE_CHANGED` → N echoes → N more handlers — an event explosion that makes the seekbar lag/jump/thrash. My in-flight suppression fixed the *visual* flicker but not this stacking (which predates it). This asymmetry (two of the three attach calls guarded) is the smoking gun.

**Fix (primary):** give `attach_control_events` the same idempotency guard (`attached_controls: HashSet<u32>`) so control signals attach once per node, mirroring the other two. (Secondary, if you also see it: `GtkScale`'s `value_changed` also fires on programmatic `set_value` — after the guard, one echo round-trip per change is already broken by app-side equality suppression.)

## Plan

**Workstream 1 — Option A: TUI in-flight guard** (on `feat/ratatui-renderer`)
1. Merge `main` into the branch (2 behind: the seekbar commit + PR #113 merge) so it has the `spec/EVENTS.md` "In-flight interaction" section.
2. `pathland-render-tui/src/render.rs`: `active_value: Option<(u32, f32)>` + `begin/update/end_value_interaction`; `draw_slider` prefers it over node `VALUE` while a slider is active; `on_mouse` marks on press / clears on release; **no** drag-scrubbing emission. Tests: active slider ignores an inbound `VALUE` change, applies it after release. status.md note.
3. Commit on the branch.

**Workstream 2 — fix the broken seekbar** (new branch from `main`, e.g. `fix/seekbar-control-attach`, since `fix/seekbar-issue`'s remote is gone)
1. Add the `attached_controls` idempotency guard to `attach_control_events`.
2. A small pure-decision test (`should_attach_control(attached)`) + keep the widget tests green.
3. `cargo test`, `npm test`+typecheck, `mvn -q install`, commit.

content.text:
Found it. This is a **server-side Quarkus WebSocket send bug**, distinct from the flicker fix (which was client-side and merged). Here's the diagnosis.

## Root cause — Quarkus swallows send failures; Java sends unbuffered

**1. `QuarkusConnection.send` swallows every failure** (`QuarkusConnection.java:16-18`):
```java
connection.sendBinary(bytes).subscribe().with(ignored -> {}, failure -> {});
```
The `failure -> {}` discards errors. `PathlandSession.send` (`PathlandSession.java:131-143`) only clears the connection when `conn.send` **throws** or `!conn.isOpen()` — with the swallow, neither ever fires, so the session keeps "sending" into a broken path forever.

**2. The Java server sends one WS frame per signal change, unbuffered** (`PathlandSession` overrides `FrameOpcodeSink.endFrame` → `send(frame)` immediately; `FrameOpcodeSink.java:46`). A seekbar drag bursts dozens of tiny frames/sec; over a remote/slow link the Quarkus send queue overflows, `sendBinary` subscriptions fail — silently.

**Result:** the browser's WS stays "open" but the server delivers nothing → permanent freeze with **no reconnect** (the DOM client only reconnects on WS close).

**Why Quarkus but not Spring:** `SpringConnection.send` (`SpringConnection.java:17-23`) throws on failure → `PathlandSession.send` nulls the connection → Spring closes the session → the client reconnects → RESYNC recovers. The Quarkus Docker demo (docs/DEPLOY.md) is the one with the silent-stall.

## Fix plan (server-side, on a branch from main)

1. **`QuarkusConnection.send` — surface failures** (essential): on failure, close the connection (`connection.close()`), so the next `send` sees `!isOpen()` → the session clears it → the client's WS closes → it reconnects + requests RESYNC (the client already does this). Converts silent-stall into recoverable reconnect — matching Spring's behavior.
2. **Serialize sends on the Quarkus adapter**: chain `sendBinary` subscriptions (only one in flight) to avoid concurrent-subscription races during rapid deltas.
3. **Coalesce Java-side deltas** (structural, highest value): batch frames like the Rust transport's `Batcher` (flush on ~16–30 ms or a byte threshold, latest-value-wins) instead of one frame per signal change — cuts the drag burst by orders of magnitude so the queue can't overflow. Every web app benefits.
4. **Harden `PathlandSession.send`**: move `FrameCodec.encodeFrame` inside the try (it currently sits outside, so an encode exception escapes into the actor thread uncaught), and on any send failure also best-effort `connection.close()`.

**Verification:** a `PathlandSession` unit test with a failing `PathlandConnection` (send throws → connection cleared → recoverable); a `DeltaBatcher` coalescing test; `mvn test`; then a manual remote run — drag the seekbar and confirm deltas keep flowing and a forced send failure triggers client reconnect+RESYNC.

Plan finalized.

## Final plan — fix the remote Quarkus WebSocket silent-stop

Branch: new from `main` (e.g. `fix/ws-send-recovery`).

**1. `QuarkusConnection.send` — surface failures** (`pathland-quarkus-starter/.../QuarkusConnection.java:16-18`)
```java
connection.sendBinary(bytes).subscribe().with(
    ignored -> {},
    failure -> { try { connection.close(); } catch (Exception ignored) {} });
```
On failure the connection closes → next `PathlandSession.send` sees `!isOpen()` → clears it → the DOM client's WS closes → it reconnects + sends `META::RESYNC` → the new session re-syncs. (Matches Spring's recoverable behavior.)

**2. Serialize sends on the Quarkus adapter** — a small send-chain (only one `sendBinary` subscription in flight; subsequent sends queue behind it) to avoid concurrent-subscription races during rapid deltas.

**3. Coalesce Java-side deltas** — new `DeltaBatcher` in `pathland-server-core` (`PathlandSession`): `FrameOpcodeSink.endFrame` enqueues instead of sending immediately; flush on a ~16–30 ms timer or a byte threshold (latest-value-wins for intermediate `VALUE` deltas), mirroring the Rust transport's `Batcher` (`max_interval`/`max_batch_bytes`). Drastically cuts the drag burst and general WS churn.

**4. Harden `PathlandSession.send`** (`PathlandSession.java:131-143`) — move `FrameCodec.encodeFrame(frame)` inside the `try` (an encode exception currently escapes into the actor thread), and on any send failure best-effort `connection.close()` in addition to clearing the connection.

**Verification**
- `PathlandSession` unit test with a failing `PathlandConnection`: send throws → connection cleared → session stops sending; a later `connect()`/resync works.
- `DeltaBatcher` test: N frames in a window → ≤ M sends, intermediate `VALUE` deltas collapse to the latest.
- `mvn -q install -DskipTests` reactor green (cargo/npm untouched — client-side in-flight fix already merged).
- Manual: run the Quarkus demo (Docker or `quarkus:dev`), drag the seekbar remotely; confirm deltas keep flowing and a forced send failure (or `kill`-style network break) triggers client reconnect + RESYNC.

Note: this is a separate, pre-existing server bug — the merged in-flight flicker fix (client-side) doesn't touch the send path; the drag burst simply exposes it.

Ready to execute on your go.
Go on a new branch.

content.text:
Done. The remote WebSocket silent-stop is fixed on `fix/ws-send-recovery`.

## What was wrong
The **Quarkus** WebSocket adapter swallowed every send failure (`failure -> {}`), so `PathlandSession` never learned deliveries stopped. Meanwhile the Java server sent **one tiny WS frame per signal change, unbuffered** — a seekbar drag bursts dozens of frames/sec, which overflows the send queue on a remote/slow link. Result: the browser's WS stayed "open" but the server delivered nothing, and the DOM client never reconnects (it only reconnects on close).

## What landed (all four)
1. **`QuarkusConnection`** — sends are now **serialized** (one `sendBinary` subscription in flight, rest queued), and a **send failure closes the connection** → the session drops it → the client's WS closes → it reconnects + requests `META::RESYNC`. Recoverable instead of silent-stall.
2. **`DeltaBatcher`** (new, `pathland-server-core`) — merges per-signal frames (opcodes + a single **rebased string section**) into one network batch, flushed ~20 ms or 16 KB — the Java analogue of the Rust `Batcher`. A drag burst collapses to ~50 messages/sec. Wired into `PathlandSession`'s `endFrame` (only for live, connected sessions).
3. **`PathlandSession.sendBatch`** — dropped connection on any send failure (+ best-effort close); `resync()` flushes immediately; `close()` shuts down the batcher.
4. **status.md** updates for `pathland-server-core` + the Quarkus starter.

## Verified
`mvn` reactor tests green — `PathlandSessionTest` 9 (incl. new *drops failed connection + recovers on reconnect*), `DeltaBatcherTest` 2 (rebased-string merge + 100-frame burst → 1 send). No Rust/TS changes.

## To try it
Rebuild the demo (`cargo build -p pathland-render-html` if needed, then `./scripts/run-quarkus-demo.sh`), host it remotely, drag the seekbar — deltas keep flowing, and a network break now recovers via reconnect+RESYNC instead of freezing.

content.text:
Yes — **Spring Boot already gets the burst handling**, because both fixes live in the shared `pathland-server-core` that every starter uses:

1. **`DeltaBatcher` coalescing** — wired into the shared `PathlandSession`, so Spring's `PathlandSocket` (→ `PathlandRegistry` → `PathlandSession`) collapses a drag burst into ~50 coalesced messages/sec just like Quarkus. No per-framework change needed.
2. **Send-failure recovery** — `sendBatch` drops the connection on failure; Spring's `session.sendMessage` **throws** on failure (it never swallowed), so a slow/overflowing Spring client → connection dropped → client reconnects + `META::RESYNC`. Spring already recovered from this; it still does.
3. **Side benefit my change added for Spring**: before, Spring's **blocking** `sendMessage` ran synchronously on the shared `pathland-actor` thread (from `endFrame`) — a slow remote client would block the single actor and stall **every session**. Now sends run on the batcher's **per-session** scheduler thread, so a slow Spring client only stalls its own session's flush.

**What Spring still lacks vs. Quarkus** (and what it doesn't need):
- The Quarkus serialized-send queue — not needed: Spring's `sendMessage` is already synchronous and internally serialized, and the batcher calls it from one thread per session.
- **Optional hardening for very slow clients**: Spring's `sendMessage` blocks; if a client stalls, its batcher thread blocks and that session's pending delta memory can grow (bounded by a reconnect, since the actor stays free). The idiomatic Spring fix is wrapping the session in `ConcurrentWebSocketSessionDecorator` (from `spring-websocket`, already on the classpath via `spring-boot-starter-websocket`) — buffers while a send is in progress and drops/closes on buffer/time limits, so extreme backpressure becomes a clean close→reconnect instead of unbounded memory.

So: bursts **are** handled for Spring today; the only optional follow-up is Spring-specific **backpressure buffering** for pathological slow clients. Want me to add the `ConcurrentWebSocketSessionDecorator` hardening to `SpringConnection` as a small follow-up on this branch?

Confirmed: the three copies are **byte-identical** (same md5s, same ~9 MB total), all demo modules depend on `pathland-demo-views`, and the asset URL references (`/_pathland/assets/...`) live in the shared views (string assertions only — no file deps). So dedup is safe and clean.

# Plan — embed the demo assets once in `pathland-demo-views`

## Approach
Move the 18 assets (6 audio, 6 covers, 6 lyrics) into the shared project at
`lib/java/pathland-demo-views/src/main/resources/META-INF/resources/_pathland/assets/{audio,albumart,lyrics}/`

`META-INF/resources/` is the **standard location both web frameworks serve from dependency jars automatically**:
- **Spring Boot** default static locations include `classpath:/META-INF/resources/` (scans all jars on the classpath).
- **Quarkus** merges `META-INF/resources/` from the app + all dependency jars.

So the Quarkus and Spring demos keep serving `/_pathland/assets/...` with **zero code changes** — the demo-views jar (already a dependency of all three) now supplies them.

## Steps
1. **Move** the 18 files from the quarkus copy into `pathland-demo-views/src/main/resources/META-INF/resources/_pathland/assets/` (Maven includes `src/main/resources` in the jar automatically — no pom change).
2. **Delete** the three duplicate trees:
   - `pathland-quarkus-demo/.../META-INF/resources/_pathland/assets/`
   - `pathland-spring-boot-demo/.../static/_pathland/assets/`
   - `pathland-gtk-demo/.../resources/assets/`
3. **Update `GtkHost`** (`pathland-gtk-demo`): change the extraction source from its own `/assets/...` to the shared jar copy — `getResourceAsStream("/META-INF/resources/_pathland/" + path)`, keeping `ASSET_FILES` entries (`assets/audio/track1.mp3`, …) so the extracted layout under the asset root stays `assets/…` and `/_pathland/assets/x` → `<root>/assets/x` still resolves unchanged.
4. **Add a regression test** in `pathland-demo-views`: assert all 18 resources resolve on the classpath (`getResourceAsStream(...) != null`), so a missing/renamed asset fails the build instead of a silent 404 in the demos.
5. **Verify**
   - `mvn -q install -DskipTests` (reactor; demo-views jar now embeds the assets).
   - Run the Quarkus + Spring demos; `curl -I http://localhost:8080/_pathland/assets/audio/track1.mp3` → 200.
   - GTK demo extraction resolves from the jar.
   - `mvn test` for `pathland-demo-views` + `pathland-render-html` (its SSR test only asserts URL strings — unaffected).

## Notes / tradeoffs
- `META-INF/resources/` is chosen over a jar-root `assets/` because both web frameworks serve it from dependencies **without custom resource handlers/routes** (the alternative needs per-framework wiring for no benefit).
- The TUI demo (`pathland-tui-demo`) doesn't render media — no change.
- Net result: ~9 MB stored once instead of three times; the demos shrink accordingly.

One decision to confirm:

Title: Classloader optimisations for resource loading
URL: https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/13256
Published: N/A
Author: N/A
Highlights:
**Description** 
This is about optimising how our (production) classloader `RunnerClassLoader` can efficiently open resources, and release the internal caches so to keep using a minimal footprint. 
 
**Implementation ideas** 
Vertx has a caching layer implemented by `io.vertx.core.file.impl.FileResolver`, which will trigger loading the full list of resources of any parent directory as well when a single resource is requested, as it attempts to then create a cache on filesystem. 
 
This is an interestin idea, but it doesn't play along well with the current implementation of the Quarkus `RunnerClassLoader`, as attempting to load e.g. `META-INF/resources/` will trigger the load on all jars which have such a resource path (which means opening many jar files). 
 
Following up on ideas discussed in #13219 , some options IMO worth considering: 
 
 - pre-load all the resources during boot, keep them in memory (and disable the Vertx FS-cache ?) 
 - actually leverage the `io.vertx.core.file.impl.FileResolver` explicitly during boot to build up the cache on filesystem, then release all caches 
 - extract the "hot resources" during build of the application into the filesystem? (For example static webpages?) 
 - we could opt to be more fine-grained indexing in the map _packages/ClassLoadingResource_ in `RunnerClassLoader`, specifically for resources to have more precision - so to hit the right jar files. 
 
## StaticResourcesBuildItem 
 
We could also take this opportunity to actually process the resources which have been explicitly mentioned by `StaticResourcesBuildItem` more optimally, and fallback to a "slow mode" (existing?) for any unlisted resource. 
 
This could be an opportunity to provide a warning about the need of a resource being loaded, as this would fail in native mode. 
 
## ServiceProviderBuildItem 
 
Similarly services from `META-INF/services/` could be specifically optimised, and we can take advantage of having a fallback mode in JVM which would produce a warning for native mode. 
 
## Testing for proper resource configuration 
 
To make it more obvious that there's a missing resource registration, I'd also propose having an environment flag which upgrades the warning into an exception. 
This would be useful during testing; although I believe it's probably best left as an opt-in to not nag people too much - especially as they might not be interested in extreme optimisations and/or native images. 
 
 
 
 

## Timeline

content.text:
Diagnosis complete. Here's what's happening and the plan.

## Root cause
The dedup moved the assets from each web demo's **own** `META-INF/resources` (served from the app's filesystem — fast, OS-cached) into the shared `pathland-demo-views` **dependency jar**. Quarkus/Spring now serve `/_pathland/assets/*` **from inside the jar**:

- Every request (including the `<audio>` element's `Range` requests for seeking/buffering) reads and inflates the jar entry; media-serving from a jar isn't range/streaming-friendly, so seeking and buffering stall.
- Neither demo sets static caching config — Spring sends **no `Cache-Control`** by default, so the browser re-downloads.
- The new **128 kbps mono** tracks are ~**2× larger** than the old placeholders (~2.6–2.9 MB each, ~16 MB total audio), amplifying it on a remote host.

## Recommended fix (keeps the single embedded copy)
Serve the assets from **disk with proper headers**, extracted once from the demo-views jar at startup — the same pattern the GTK host already uses:

1. **`pathland-demo-views`**: add a `DemoAssets.extractToTemp()` helper that unpacks the 24 assets from the classpath to a temp dir (`<root>/assets/…`); single implementation, and `GtkHost.extractAssets` delegates to it.
2. **Quarkus demo**: a startup bean that registers a Vert.x `StaticHandler` at `/_pathland/assets/*` → `<root>/assets` — disk serving with `Range` support (audio seek), `Content-Length`, and caching headers.
3. **Spring demo**: register `file:<root>/assets` in Spring's static locations (a `WebMvcConfigurer`) — same benefits.
4. Optionally tune caching (`quarkus.http.static-resources.max-age` / Spring `spring.web.resources.cache.period`).
5. **Verify**: run the Quarkus demo; `curl -I …/audio/track1.mp3` (200, `Accept-Ranges: bytes`), `curl -H "Range: bytes=0-1023"` → **206**, and time it; confirm seeking works. Do the same for Spring.

## Fallback (minimal, reverts part of the dedup)
Re-embed the assets in each web demo's own `META-INF/resources` again (fast app-local serving) and keep the demo-views copy only for GTK. Contradicts the dedup goal.

Two questions before I finalize:

content.text:
Plan finalized.

## Final plan — fast disk-backed asset serving (Quarkus + Spring), single embedded copy kept

**1. `pathland-demo-views` — `DemoAssets` helper** (`com.pathland.demo.assets`)
- `DemoAssets.extractToTemp()`: unpacks the 24 assets from the classpath (`/META-INF/resources/_pathland/assets/…`) into a fresh temp dir (`<root>/assets/…`), overwriting; returns the root. Shares its asset list with `DemoAssetsTest`.
- `GtkHost.extractAssets()` delegates to it (asset root = the returned root) — one extraction implementation for all hosts.

**2. Quarkus demo** — serve from disk

Done — the slow Quarkus asset serving is fixed, committed `758b3f7e` on `refactor/shared-demo-assets`.

## What changed
The assets stay **single-embedded** in `pathland-demo-views`, but are now served from **disk** instead of from inside the jar:

- **`DemoAssets`** (`pathland-demo-views`): `extractToTemp()` unpacks all 24 assets once at startup to `<root>/assets/…`; `GtkHost` now delegates to it (same asset-root semantics). `DemoAssetsTest` guards the 24 assets + the extraction.

- **Spring**: same — `206` on range, full track in **5.7 ms** (vs the previous jar-based stalls on a remote host).
- `mvn -q clean install` reactor green; demo-views 16 tests + gtk-demo 6 pass.

Audio seeking now works (Range), and the browser caches media. The svg icons serve fine (no `Content-Type` from Vert.x — same as before, not a regression).

Confirmed — `io.vertx.ext.web.handler.FileSystemAccess.ROOT` exists in vertx-web 4.5.32.

## Plan — fix the Quarkus startup failure

**Root cause** (`DemoAssetsRoute.java:34`): `StaticHandler.create("<absolute path>")` rejects a `/`-prefixed filesystem root (`root cannot start with '/'`) — Vert.x's `create(String)` treats the argument as a *web* root, not an absolute path, unless you grant root filesystem access.

**Fix** — one-line change in `DemoAssetsRoute.onStart`:
```java
import io.vertx.ext.web.handler.FileSystemAccess;
...
router.route("/_pathland/assets/*")
      .order(-10)
      .handler(StaticHandler.create(FileSystemAccess.ROOT, root.resolve("assets").toString()));
```
This serves the extracted temp dir from disk with the same `Range` + caching behavior (Vert.x's native API for absolute roots). The Spring side is unaffected — it uses Spring's `file:` resource handler, which has no such validation (already verified serving 200/206 earlier).

3. `curl -I …/_pathland/assets/audio/track1.mp3` → 200, `accept-ranges: bytes`, `content-length`, `cache-control`; `Range: bytes=0-1023` → **206**; timing.
4. Commit on `refactor/shared-demo-assets`.

content.text:
Fixed and committed `de004dc5`.

## Root cause
It wasn't a path problem — the Spring starter's `PathlandIndexController.framework` maps `/_pathland/**` (a `@Controller`, order 0) and serves `static/_pathland/<file>` from the classpath. That controller **preempted** my `DemoAssetsConfig` resource handler (which runs at lowest precedence), and since the assets had moved out of `static/_pathland/` into the demo-views jar, it returned **404**.

## What changed
- **Starter (`PathlandIndexController`)** — generalized to serve a configured **`pathland.asset-dir`** filesystem root under `/_pathland/**` (traversal-guarded), falling back after the classpath bundle lookup. Reuses its existing `Range` logic (now on a `Resource`), and adds `Cache-Control: max-age=604800, public, immutable` to the full + range responses.
- **Spring demo (`SpringDemoApplication.main`)** — sets `pathland.asset-dir` = `DemoAssets.extractToTemp()` before boot (single embedded copy, extracted once).
- **Deleted** the broken `DemoAssetsConfig` (`WebMvcConfigurer`).

## Verified (fresh build + packaged run)
- `/_pathland/assets/audio/track1.mp3` → **200**, `Content-Type: audio/mpeg`, `Content-Length`, `Accept-Ranges`, `Cache-Control`.
- `Range: bytes=0-1023` → **206** `Content-Range: bytes 0-1023/2841747`.
- `/_pathland/dom-renderer.js` still **200**; the mounted `/app2/_pathland/assets/…` also **200**.
- Full 2.8 MB track in **6 ms**.
- Reactor tests green (`mvn -q test`, excluding the two web demos).

Quarkus is unaffected (its `DemoAssetsRoute` was already fixed). Both web demos now serve the assets fast from disk with working audio seeking.

content.text:
## Analysis — does a built-in ACK make sense?

**Yes, but only for the failure modes TCP can't cover.** On a single live WebSocket, TCP already guarantees ordering and no loss — a server→client delta can't vanish while the connection is genuinely up. The real "messages lost silently" cases are:

1. **Half-open / silently-broken connections** (NAT/keepalive drop, proxy frame loss, dead peer): the server keeps sending into a socket that "looks" open — deltas are never delivered and **no close is detected**, so the existing reconnect + `META::RESYNC` never fires. This is your "updates not received."
2. **Client→server events lost** into such a connection: browser `send()` is optimistic (no throw), so an important `VALUE_CHANGED`/`TEXT_CHANGED` is dropped server-side and **neither side notices** — your "events not received."
3. **Detected drops** — already handled: reconnect + `RESYNC` (full snapshot).

So the ACK's job is to make delivery **observable** and trigger the existing recovery paths, not to add per-message replay. The protocol already has the seam for it: the PLPL batch header carries `frameCount` (spec/OPCODE.md:651) — the Java server currently stamps **0**, and the TS transport even has a "P3: frameCount gap handling" hook (`transport.ts:4`).

## Proposed design (phased)

**Phase 1 — server→client delivery + liveness**
- Server stamps each flushed batch with a **per-session monotonic `frameCount`** (`DeltaBatcher`/`PathlandSession`).
- Client tracks the **highest contiguous applied frameCount** and sends a throttled **`META::ACK`** (new, host→guest) with it — also serves as a heartbeat.
- Server: an **ack gap** (client behind while the connection is up) → server sends a server-driven `META::RESYNC` (reuses the snapshot path); an **ack timeout** (silence) → close → client reconnects + `RESYNC`. Converts silent loss into recovery.

**Phase 2 — client→server event reliability**
- Client stamps each outbound event batch with a per-connection sequence and **buffers unacked events** (latest-per-control is enough — events are idempotent).
- Server ACKs the last processed client sequence (piggybacked); the client drops acked events and **resends unacked on reconnect** before/after `RESYNC`.

**Phase 3 — client-side liveness (hardening)**: the client also reconnects if the server is silent (server heartbeat or read timeout), so a dead server is detected on both ends.

**Protocol (spec-first)**: `META::ACK = 0x04` in `spec/OPCODE.md` + `pathland-core` constants + a conformance vector; document the frameCount-sequencing/ack semantics in the network-batch section.

**Surface**: Rust core (constant), Java (`Commands.Meta`, `FrameCodec` ack + `encodeFrame(frameCount)`, session/batcher sequencing + gap/liveness), TS (`plpl`/`events`/`transport`/`index`), no Quarkus/Spring adapter changes (recovery lives in the session).

Plan finalized (all three phases, replay-buffer recovery, both directions).

## Final plan — built-in ACK / reliability for the socket transport

New branch from `main` (e.g. `feat/ws-ack-reliability`).

### Protocol (spec-first)
1. **`META::ACK = 0x04`** (both directions; `spec/OPCODE.md` + `pathland-core` constant + `Commands.Meta.ACK` + a `spec/CONFORMANCE.md` golden vector). `A` = the highest contiguous sequence counter of the **peer's** stream this side has processed:
   - **client→server**: ACKs server frame batches (recovery + liveness).
   - **server→client**: ACKs the client's event sequence (lets the client drop its retransmit buffer; doubles as the heartbeat).
2. **Sequencing contract** (documented in the network-batch section): every server→client batch carries a per-session monotonic `frameCount` (the field already exists — currently 0); every client→server event batch carries a per-connection monotonic event sequence (its `frameCount`).
3. Direction/flags already distinguish the two.

### Server (`pathland-server-core`)
- **Sequencing**: `PathlandSession`/`DeltaBatcher` stamps each flushed batch with an incrementing `frameCount` (`FrameCodec.encodeFrame(frame, frameCount)`).
- **Replay buffer** (bounded ring, ~last 64 frames / ~256 KB): keeps each sent batch; evicted as the client ACKs. On an ACK **gap** → replay `ack+1..lastSent` in order; if the gap exceeds the buffer → fall back to a server-driven `META::RESYNC`.
- **Liveness**: per-session `lastClientActivity`; no ACK/message within ~30 s → drop the connection (client reconnects + RESYNC). The existing Quarkus send-failure-close stays.
- **Event ACK**: track the last processed client event sequence; emit a `META::ACK` (server→client) in the next batch and on a periodic idle heartbeat, so the client can flush its buffer.

### Client (`lib/typescript`)
- Track the highest **contiguous applied** `frameCount`; send throttled `META::ACK` (~250 ms) + as an idle heartbeat.
- Stamp outbound event batches with an event sequence; **buffer unacked events** (latest-per-control, bounded); drop acked on the server's `META::ACK`; **resend unacked on reconnect** (events are idempotent).
- **Read-timeout liveness**: no server message within ~15–30 s → close → reconnect + RESYNC (catches a dead server on the client side too).

### Verification
- Rust: core constant + conformance vector.
- Java: batcher stamps increasing frameCount; replay-on-gap (fake connection records re-sent frames); buffer-overflow → RESYNC fallback; ack-timeout closes; server→client ACK emitted.
- TS: applied-frameCount tracking; throttled ACK; reconnect resends unacked events; read-timeout triggers reconnect.
- `cargo test`, `npm test` + typecheck, `mvn -q clean install`; then a live flaky-link check (throttle/simulate drops) against the Quarkus demo.

### Notes / tradeoffs
- No per-message retransmission of server deltas beyond the bounded replay buffer; the client is the recovery trigger for everything it can detect, the server for what only it can see.
- Replayed frames are safe: TCP ordering means the client never applies anything beyond its ack, so replay delivers exactly the missing frames (no duplicates on a live connection; reconnect is deduped by RESYNC).
- `status.md` updates for `pathland-core`, `pathland-server-core`, `lib/typescript`.

Your theory is confirmed — here's the exact loop and the plan.

## Root cause (confirmed)
1. The renderer reports `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED(seconds)` ~1/s.
2. The demo binds `Audio.of(...).position(position)` — **MEDIA_POSITION is bound to the same `position` signal** that `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` feeds (`PlayerBar.java:44`).
3. So every time update → `position.set(seconds)` → re-emits `SET_PROPERTY MEDIA_POSITION = seconds`.
4. The renderer applies it; the echo guard compares against **`currentTime`** (`should_seek` GTK `lib.rs:1344`, TS `apply.ts:1217`: `|currentTime - target| > 0.25`). With network delay > 0.25 s the delayed echo is > 0.25 behind real time → the player **seeks backward every second** → jitter.

The guard is distance-vs-current, so it fails exactly when the network is the problem.

## Plan — three layers

**1. Renderer echo guard → compare against the last-*reported* position (GTK + TS)** — fixes the symptom regardless of app behavior:
- GTK: `should_seek(now, target)` → compare `target` against the `MediaPlayer`'s `last_reported` (needs adding that field to the struct; it exists as a local `Rc<Cell>` at `lib.rs:681`).
- TS: `apply.ts:1217` → `Math.abs(state.lastReported - target) > 0.25`.
- Why robust: the echo *is* the last-reported position (just delayed), so `|echo − lastReported| ≈ 0` → always suppressed at any delay; a real seek to a different position still fires. Only a seek within 0.25 s of the last report is suppressed (effectively a no-op).

**2. Demo decoupling (Java) — the correct architecture**, removes the echo traffic entirely:
- New `seekRequest` signal bound to `Audio.position(seekRequest)` (MEDIA_POSITION).
- `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` keeps feeding the display `position` signal (seekbar thumb) **only**.
- The seek slider's drag writes **both** `position` (immediate display) and `seekRequest` (the seek command) — a small `PercentSeek`-style wrapper whose `set` writes both.
- Result: `MEDIA_POSITION` is emitted **only on user seeks**, never as a per-second echo.

**3. Spec** (`spec/EVENTS.md` Media): document that **`MEDIA_POSITION` is a seek *command*** (app→renderer, on user seek) while **`MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` is a position *report*** (renderer→app); apps MUST NOT bind the command to the report signal; renderers MUST suppress a `MEDIA_POSITION` write within an epsilon of their last-reported position (echo guard, defense-in-depth).

**Verification:** GTK `should_seek` decision test; TS test (echo within `lastReported` → no seek, real seek → seek); demo test (`MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` emits no `MEDIA_POSITION`; a slider drag does); `cargo test`, `npm test`, `mvn -q clean install`; live audio check on both demos.

input.newString:
- **`MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED`**: the media's current playback position in seconds.
  Reported **when the playback position advances ~1 second** (at most ~1/s)
  while playing; a seek initiated by the app (`MEDIA_POSITION` change) is not
  echoed back.
- **Commands vs reports (MUST)**: `MEDIA_POSITION`/`MEDIA_VOLUME` are **seek /
  volume commands** the app writes to control playback; `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` /
  `MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED` are **position / volume reports** the renderer emits.
  An app **MUST NOT** bind a command property to the signal its matching report
  updates — that echoes every report back as a command (e.g. each second's
  position report re-emits a `MEDIA_POSITION` seek, causing per-second seek
  jitter). The app binds the command to a **user-interaction-only** signal and
  routes the report to a separate display signal.
- **Renderer echo guard (MUST)**: a renderer **MUST NOT** act on a command write
  that matches the value it last **reported** (within an epsilon): the app is
  echoing the report back, not interacting. E.g. a `MEDIA_POSITION` write within
  `0.25 s` of the last `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` must not seek; a `MEDIA_VOLUME`
  write within `0.01` of the last `MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED` must not re-apply. This
  is defense-in-depth: it holds at **any** network latency (the echo *is* the
  last-reported value), so a delayed echo cannot fight the playback position.
- **Guards**: media events flow only when the app bound the matching control
  property (`PLAYBACK_STATE`/`MEDIA_POSITION`/`MEDIA_VOLUME`) on the node; a
  plain renderer-native media element reports nothing.
